executive_summary: The defining thread of today is the fracturing of Republican unity under the weight of competing pressures from Trump's agenda and institutional resistance within the party's own ranks. Senate Republicans defying Trump, as noted in The Economist, combined with House Republicans pulling a planned vote on Iran and stalling key budget votes, reveals a GOP caucus increasingly unable to deliver on either foreign policy or fiscal priorities. The Foreign Affairs framing of Iran as Vietnam is particularly resonant here — it suggests the administration's Iran posture carries the same intraparty and public legitimacy risks that have historically broken presidencies. This breakdown matters not because of any single vote, but because it signals a structural loss of legislative momentum at a moment when the White House needs congressional alignment most. If Republican lawmakers are willing to openly defy Trump on both war powers and spending in the same day, the governing coalition that was supposed to define this term is under serious strain.

newsletters.title: The Morning: Get ready to grill

items.headline: People get ready
items.blurb: Monday is a somber, important holiday, one that honors those who gave their lives in service to the nation. But Americans are prone to celebration, even in the face of mourning. Many will light grills this weekend, ice down cases of beer, turn up the music and gather with family and friends for good eating and endless debate: Is this a barbecue or a cookout?

items.headline: Beer brats and beer-can chicken for the long weekend
items.blurb: When it comes to long-weekend cooking, you don't have to choose a stretch assignment. Me, I'm thinking beer brats for at least one meal. items.headline: Mourning one of sports' best
items.blurb: NASCAR star Kyle Busch is dead at 41, a sentence still hard to believe nearly a full day after the news broke. He leaves behind two children, ages 4 and 11, and a legacy like no other in racing. His death is shocking for both the sport he helped shape over the last 20 years and due to the nature of it: Busch went to the hospital this week with an unspecified illness and never recovered. What a tragedy.

newsletters.title: The US in Brief: Senate Republicans defy Trump

items.headline: Senate Republicans defy Trump over Anti-Weaponisation Fund
items.blurb: In a rare act of defiance to Donald Trump, Senate Republicans postponed a vote on a bill funding his immigration crackdown because some objected to his "Anti-Weaponisation Fund". Senators said officials had not explained who could receive payouts and whether people convicted of crimes related to the storming of the Capitol on January 6th 2021 might benefit. Party leaders had already removed funding tied to Mr Trump's White House ballroom from the immigration bill, for fear the rank-and-file would not support it.

items.headline: Trump postpones AI executive order
items.blurb: Mr Trump abruptly postponed the signing of an executive order that would have expanded federal oversight of artificial-intelligence models, including by requiring AI firms to share new models with the government before release. David Sacks, Mr Trump's former AI adviser, reportedly helped persuade the president to pull back. Mr Trump said it "gets in the way" of America's tech race with China.

items.headline: Gavin Newsom orders California to prepare for AI-caused layoffs
items.blurb: As Mr Trump was arguing that AI was "bringing in a lot of jobs", Gavin Newsom, California's Democratic governor, ordered state agencies to prepare for "potential layoffs and economic disruption" caused by AI. California's state agencies will explore new unemployment-insurance and severance policies for displaced workers.

items.headline: House Republicans cancel vote on limiting Trump's war powers against Iran
items.blurb: Republican leaders in the House of Representatives cancelled a vote on whether to limit Mr Trump's ability to wage war on Iran without congressional approval after concluding the measure might pass. Several Republicans had defected on a similar vote last week, which failed in a 212-212 tie. This week several Republican senators backed a similar measure.

items.headline: DNC post-mortem blames Kamala Harris for 2024 election loss
items.blurb: A draft of the Democratic National Convention's post-mortem of the presidential election in 2024 concluded that Kamala Harris failed to distance herself sufficiently from Joe Biden and did not make a strong enough case against Mr Trump. It also blamed her for responding inadequately to an advertisement attacking her support for taxpayer-funded gender-transition surgery for prisoners. The chairman of the DNC released the draft after CNN obtained it, but said he did not endorse its conclusions.

items.headline: Stephen Colbert hosts final episode of The Late Show
items.blurb: Stephen Colbert hosted his final episode of CBS's "The Late Show" after 11 years at the helm of one of America's best-known talk shows. In the Trump era, Mr Colbert's acerbic monologues helped him top the ratings. His cancellation was controversial; critics accused CBS of yielding to pressure from the president.

breaking_digest.narrative:
House Republicans faced a turbulent day on Capitol Hill, pulling a planned vote to end the war in Iran late Wednesday evening [1], while earlier in the day the party also delayed key budget votes as members pushed back against a Trump-backed spending provision [3]. The twin setbacks signal growing intraparty friction over both foreign policy and fiscal priorities.

In other news, Tennessee called off a scheduled execution Wednesday after staff were unable to locate a suitable vein on the condemned prisoner [4]. Separately, NASCAR mourned the death of two-time Cup Series champion Kyle Busch, who died at age 41 [2]. No cause of death was immediately specified.
